answer: Because the canyon record is per identity, the atlas audit recounts the streak and a reset is visible in the ledger. Promotion out of probation presupposes 4 consecutive epochs with no upheld complaint, so a single bad verdict resets the clock entirely. That makes a farm's early mistakes expensive in a way that compounds, because each duplicate self restarts separately and none of them can inherit another's tide standing. That is 9 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
